source.title: Grokking as a Phase Transition between Competing Basins: a Singular Learning Theory Approach
source.authors: B. Cullen; Sergio Estan-Ruiz; Riya Danait; Jiayi Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Its title in the text differs from the supplied metadata title; the document is otherwise relevant.
record.tranche_reason: It measures delayed generalisation on modular addition and LLC trajectories, but uses a two-layer quadratic network and an LLC-based analysis rather than reproducing the original study’s method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training/validation accuracy and LLC results. Findings attributed to earlier work in the related-work section are not recorded as rows. The appendix describes additional plotted sweeps, but the extracted text does not provide their individual plotted values.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own two-layer quadratic network on modular addition (p=53). It reports delayed generalisation, with training accuracy saturating early and validation accuracy rising sharply much later. It also tracks a training-data-only progress measure, the LLC, across the transition. The method differs from the originals (quadratic net, centred squared loss, SLT analysis), so it is T2.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right. The authors cast grokking as a transition from a higher-LLC memorising basin to a lower-LLC generalising basin, and derive closed-form LLCs for quadratic networks. They show training-data LLC trajectories track, and peak before, the generalisation transition. They admit the link to SGD dynamics is incomplete, and that the late-stage LLC formula is a generic reference value.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition but a two-layer quadratic network with regression-style squared loss and an LLC analysis; it does not reproduce the original grokking study’s method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that LLC estimates vary by orders of magnitude with the SGLD localization parameter and sampler learning rate, and advises holding sampler hyperparameters fixed for comparisons. It also reports that grokking severity decreases as learning rate increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking severity (cumulative train–validation accuracy gap) decreases markedly as learning rate increases. Larger learning rates also coincide with smaller peak LLC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The severity of the grokking delay is modulated by optimisation hyperparameters such as learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: The Hessian trace tracks the LLC through the grokking transition but rises after generalisation while the LLC keeps falling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curvature-based probes track the grokking transition but diverge from degeneracy measures after it.

fits_no_version.finding: The final LLC grows linearly with width K and with p, even though all widths generalise. The authors read this as wider models not being the small solution plus redundant neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalising solutions differ in effective complexity across widths rather than being one width-invariant structure.

record.problems: The core trajectory result is presented for a specified modular-addition setting; exact accuracy and LLC values are not stated in the text. LLC estimates are highly sensitive to sampler/localization settings. The authors describe the SGD connection as incomplete and the late-stage LLC formula as a generic reference subject to assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix H.2 Figures 5–8 and H.4 Figures 10–11 show additional dataset, width, weight-decay, and learning-rate sweeps, but the extracted text provides captions rather than individual plotted values or condition-specific outcomes. No separate rows were made for those plots.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks: the training fraction is fixed at 0.4 and no data-fraction sweep is reported.
Formation of a generalising circuit (e.g. Fourier features) and later removal of memorising components; no mechanistic analysis is done.
Non-algorithmic data and initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich switching are not tested empirically; the lazy-versus-feature regimes appear only in the theory.
No critical dataset size and no ungrokking. A weight-decay sweep is plotted, but the text gives no condition-specific outcomes.
There is no comparison of identified algorithms across runs.
Optimizer instabilities and softmax floating-point limits are not controlled or tested.

missing.what: Robustness sweeps of the LLC/generalisation tracking across p (53, 61, 71), hidden width (600–1000), weight decay (1e-4 to 1e-5) and learning rate (1e-4 to 1e-2). Only captions are available, with no stated outcomes.
GSM versus learning rate at weight decay 0, 1e-4 and 1e-5. The weight-decay-0 panel could show whether grokking occurs without weight decay.
Peak LLC versus learning rate across weight decays.
Final LLC scaling with p and width; all widths eventually generalise.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source. The evidence is mostly qualitative (figure descriptions), with no numeric accuracies or delay lengths. LLC estimates are highly sensitive to SGLD settings, which were held fixed across runs. The optimizer is not named in the extracted text. The V2 link is to the progress-measure aspect only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests delayed generalisation on modular addition, but does not test whether shrinking the training set increases the optimization delay; its reported baseline training fraction is 0.4.
Tests LLC trajectories as a progress measure, but does not identify or measure a Fourier circuit, nor measure gradual circuit formation or removal of memorizing components.
No non-algorithmic dataset or initialization-scale sweep. It varies learning rate and weight decay on modular addition, not the claimed non-algorithmic settings or lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Discusses weight decay and lower-LLC basins, but does not test whether low norm selects a more efficient circuit, or predict a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.
Does not compare whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point softmax limits, or whether controlling them removes grokking.

rows.operation_detail: Tracked a Hutchinson trace estimate alongside the LLC.

rows.note: This is a compared curvature proxy, not a measurement of circuit formation.
rows.check: This compares two probes (Hessian trace vs LLC). It is a curvature diagnostic, not a measure of circuit formation or of the grokking behaviour itself; its baseline is another probe.

rows.note: This shows that delayed-generalisation severity depends on learning rate; no GSM values are stated in the text.
rows.check: GSM falling as learning rate rises is a hyperparameter-modulation finding that no version names. It does not test the training-set-size dependence (V1), and it does not control optimizer or numerical artifacts (V7). No GSM values are stated.
